subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool routing model for cross-gateway messaging, or should this PR wait for the broader federation/identity contract tracked by the canonical issue?
rationale: The code change is not only a mechanical session-tool patch; it creates a new credentialed cross-gateway path that affects sender identity, authorization scopes, replay behavior, message delivery, and remote session ownership.

options.title: Design the federation boundary first
options.body: Keep the PR open as an implementation candidate but require the canonical issue's trust, identity, scope, and delivery contract before accepting this core API.

options.title: Proceed with a narrow peer registry
options.body: Allow the PR direction only after the raw gatewayUrl bypass, idempotency key, tokenless-peer behavior, conflicts, and real two-gateway proof are resolved.

options.title: Close this branch as the wrong shape
options.body: If maintainers do not want peer URL forwarding in core, close this PR and continue the broader federation discussion in the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Design the federation boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open as an implementation candidate but require the canonical issue's trust, identity, scope, and delivery contract before accepting this core API.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for session-tool routing and multi-agent session behavior is Peter Steinberger's prior work on this surface.
